description: HTZ Communications is ATDI's flagship software for radio network planning and spectrum engineering, used for mobile, fixed, broadcast and critical communications networks; this record covers its broadcast toolset. ATDI, based in Paris, says it has long worked with many of the world's leading broadcasters and that HTZ was used when broadcasters moved from analogue to digital radio and television (DVB-T and DAB+). For broadcast networks the software offers coverage planning, interference calculations with ITU C/I tables and net filter discrimination matrices, population analysis, ITU coordination procedures, automated site, frequency and channel assignment, single and multi-frequency network (SFN and MFN) optimisation including launch delay assignment, coexistence studies with LTE, aeronautical ILS and white-space services, microwave backhaul planning, location probability maps and power-sum methods including Monte Carlo and log-normal approximations. Technologies covered include DVB-T and T2, DVB-S and S2, ISDB-T, DTMB, MMDS, T-DAB, DAB+ and DMB, FM, IBOC and ATSC 3.0. It works with ATDI's ICS Manager and ICS Portal for coordination data. Coverage: worldwide use, with ITU procedures. Format and access: commercial desktop software under licence, with demonstrations on request. Caveats: proprietary, with results depending on the terrain, clutter and propagation models chosen. Simulation uses: coverage and interference modelling of broadcast and mobile networks, frequency planning, and assessing the coverage lost when transmitters fail. Related records: LS telcom CHIRplus_BC and Forsk Atoll are comparable suites, and the ITU-R P.1546 and P.1812 implementations give open propagation methods.
